story_ai.headline: GIFT Nifty Signals Positive Start as Global Markets and Domestic Pressures Weigh on Dalal Street
paragraphs: GIFT Nifty is at 22370, implying a positive start for the domestic session with an estimated opening gap of 6.8 points above the previous Nifty close of 22603.1. In the previous session, the Nifty finished down 1.64% at 22231.8 and Bank Nifty closed down 0.98% at 54515.05. India VIX surged 10.26% to 15.31, reflecting heightened volatility.

Overnight global cues showed pressure across major indices as S&P 500 closed down 0.47% at 7765.4 and Nasdaq dropped 1.25% to 27193.3, while Dow Jones edged up 0.1% to 51231.6. In Asia, Nikkei 225 fell 0.77% to 68512.3, Kospi lost 2.62% to 6625.9, Hang Seng rose 1.17% to 24064.0, and Shanghai dropped 1.18% to 3766.9. In Europe, DAX lost 1.18% to 24807.0 and FTSE 100 slipped 0.16% to 10441.6.

Commodities traded with mixed sentiment as Brent crude eased 0.83% to 103.41 and WTI crude fell 0.7% to 90.85. Gold gained 1.08% to 4201.8, silver rose 1.7% to 60.435, copper increased 1.2% to 6.647, and natural gas declined 1.01% to 3.136. In currency and rates, USD/INR stood at 96.78, the dollar index eased 0.11% to 102.021, and the US 10Y yield dropped 0.87% to 5.231%.

Institutional flows continue to reflect caution, with FIIs recording net sales of Rs 12943.58 crore and DIIs purchasing Rs 10703.11 crore in the cash market on 2026-10-08, bringing the 5-day FII outflow to Rs 36209.61 crore against DII inflows of Rs 35612.06 crore. Options positioning for the 2026-10-13 expiry shows a put-call ratio of 0.62 and a max pain strike at 22400.0, with prominent call walls at 23000.0, 24000.0, and 23500.0, and put walls at 21000.0, 22000.0, and 21500.0.

Today's corporate calendar features earnings results from ANANDRATHI, CANFINHOME, CANHLIFE, CORDELIA, CRAMC, INDBANK, and POONAWALLA. Stocks under the F&O ban list include AMBUJACEM, BANDHANBNK, and LICHSGFIN. Key economic events scheduled include Canadian Employment Change and Unemployment Rate alongside US Prelim UoM Consumer Sentiment and Inflation Expectations.
